Reviews of the non-invasive techniques already treat electric, magnetic, ultrasonic and optical drives as four separate physical problems
, and the clinical literature runs from non-invasive stimulation to implanted devices as a further spectrum
. This volume argues that they nonetheless share one description — a
, a cellular response, a subcellular and molecular cascade, a circuit effect, a systemic effect, an outcome — and it works through what is established, inferred and disputed at each link.
Three findings shape the volume. First,
is not intensity: the normative definition covers every parameter of the configuration that shapes the delivered field
, and yet a survey of 202 transcranial studies found 308 distinct electric-field outcome measures and no agreed metric
. Second, coupling is geometric: applied fields act first on axons and terminals, polarization depends on orientation, and the field reachable in a human brain — about 0.8
— sits at or below thresholds measured in rodents
. Third, the acting cause is often not the nominal one: the ligand that drives a
experiment is a metabolite of the compound injected
, part of the human ultrasound literature is explained by an auditory pathway rather than a cortical one
Those three findings generalise into the volume's method: state the level, state the species and

, state the dose as reported, and keep rival explanations attached to the claim rather than resolved silently. Twenty-three live disputes are catalogued on that basis, each with its rivals, the measurement that divides them and what would settle it. The closing section turns the volume's requirements into a proposed graph schema, names the ontologies that can anchor each level, and identifies the one layer where the field has a consensus
but nothing to reuse as an ontology: stimulation protocols and device parameters.

This is a scope-bounded commissioned review rather than a systematic one, written by the Manuscript Interrogator and not peer reviewed. Its literature sweep closed on 2026-09-15 and rests on 263 references, 260 of which were verified against a read abstract or full text. Volume 1 takes the first modality family in detail: vagus and cranial nerve stimulation.

children.value: This section sets out how the word "
" is used, where those uses collide, and which usage the rest of the volume adopts.
"Neuromodulation" is used for three different things. The first is a
: a current, a field or an agent that someone applies to a nervous system. The second is the physiological change that follows from that drive. The third is a class of endogenous substances, the
, and the effects they have on neurons and circuits. The clinical societies use the word mostly in the first two senses
. Cellular and circuit neuroscience uses it in the third

The first two senses are often merged in a single sentence, because a definition that says a therapy "alters nerve activity" names both the act and its result. That merge is harmless in a clinic. It is not harmless in a

The 2022 glossary produced jointly by the Neuromodulation Foundation, the Institute of Neuromodulation and the International Neuromodulation Society (INS) is the most detailed consensus source
. It extended a 2007 glossary written for
to peripheral nerve, dorsal root ganglion, deep brain and motor cortex stimulation, and defined 91 terms
. Its definition of neuromodulation is broad. Neuromodulation modifies the activity of neurons and glia by delivering an electrical, magnetic or chemical stimulus to a specific neurological target

. Two features matter here. The definition names glia as well as neurons, and it includes chemical delivery. The document is expert consensus, not an empirical study, and its scope is implanted systems
The INS's public definition, written for a lay audience, is narrower in one respect and wider in another

. It describes neuromodulation as technology that acts directly on nerves, altering nerve activity by delivering electrical or pharmaceutical agents to a target area, and it explicitly counts implanted drug pumps
. It does not mention magnetic stimulation or glia. It is a web page whose wording may change, so this volume cites it with its access date of 2026-09-15

A third consensus paper, from an international expert group led by Sivanesan and North, proposed its own definition of neuromodulation together with a classification of implantable electrical therapies for chronic pain
. It sorts those therapies by intended treatment site and clinical application, and by technical parameters that include waveform and

The three sources can be compared point by point. On which drives count, the 2022 glossary names electrical, magnetic and chemical stimuli

and the 2024 paper covers implants for pain

The two words are used side by side in the same documents. The 2022 consensus document is titled a glossary of

title: 2. Levels of organisation and the drive → outcome chain

children.value: that organises the rest of the volume, carries one example along it, and names the places where it tends to break.
The claim of this section is that every modality in the volume, device or drug, can be written as one chain:

→ cellular → subcellular/molecular → circuit → system → outcome. The drive is what is delivered. Coupling is the physical or chemical event by which the drive first changes tissue. The cellular level is what a neuron or glial cell does in response. The subcellular/molecular level is the signalling that follows, and that often outlasts the stimulus. The circuit level is how populations of connected cells change. The system level is how a whole body system, such as arousal, autonomic or immune control, changes. The outcome is what is measured in the organism. No cited paper states this seven-step chain. It is assembled from step-wise chains in two separate literatures: the brain-stimulation chain from
through local and network effects to behaviour
at the target site through target binding to pharmacological activity

Treating the chain as levels is a commitment about what counts as an explanation, not a metaphor. Churchland and Sejnowski argued that understanding perception, learning and consciousness would need methods that record large-scale brain activity together with computational models, and the article is widely cited for a scheme of
running from molecules to systems, in which an explanation has to link levels rather than stay at one
. The Atlas chain is a levels-of-organisation scheme in that sense: each link names a physical scale and a kind of entity.
The commitment has consequences, because a level cannot be read off the one below it. Marder's review of

of neuronal circuits, drawn largely from invertebrate small-circuit work, argues that neuromodulatory substances change neurons' intrinsic firing properties and effective synaptic strengths, so that the anatomical connectome is only a scaffold and the modulatory state decides which functional circuit operates
. If wiring alone does not fix circuit function, then a description of which cells a drive reaches does not fix its circuit effect. The circuit link has to be measured, or modelled, in its own right.
The same point holds for drugs. Franks's review of
argues that a small number of molecular targets account for the action of chemically diverse anaesthetics, and that the
from those targets to reversible loss of consciousness runs through the endogenous sleep and arousal circuitry, with the thalamus and the networks that regulate it at the centre
. Target and behaviour are separated by an existing physiological control circuit, not a new pathway

Modelling offers one way to connect the levels explicitly. D'Angelo and Jirsa propose combining bottom-up biophysical models of neurons and synapses with top-down network models built from functional activity, embedding detailed microcircuit models in larger assemblies to link microscopic mechanisms to macroscopic signals
. It is a programme, not a finished bridge.

Read together, these sources suggest that the chain is not a hierarchy in which the lower level fully determines the upper. It is a list of places where a separate measurement or model is needed. That is the sense in which the Atlas uses it

Why a graph forces the choices
Prose can leave much unstated; a graph edge cannot.

6.1 The borrowed vocabulary, and the preparations it came from

. They proposed it as a candidate substrate for memory
. The claim that matters here is narrower: a patterned electrical input, delivered for seconds, left synaptic transmission changed long after the input stopped
" points back to this result, obtained in an anaesthetized rabbit with an electrode on an identified fibre tract

The sign of a synaptic change was given a rule by Bienenstock, Cooper and Munro. In their formulation the size and direction of a modification depend on current postsynaptic activity relative to a threshold set by the neuron's time-averaged activity; input patterns compete rather than converging fibres

. This is a mathematical learning rule whose supporting evidence was that simulations reproduced orientation tuning and ocular-dominance patterns matching data from cats and monkeys reared normally and in altered visual environments
. The sliding threshold is a theoretical construct fitted to developmental data, not a quantity measured at a synapse
Abraham and Bear named the general case
: earlier activity changes a synapse's capacity for later LTP or
without necessarily changing its present strength
could account for some instances while other mechanisms probably contribute
. Metaplasticity is a change in a threshold, which is a different kind of node from a change in a weight

came from dissociated culture. Turrigiano and colleagues manipulated overall activity in cultured rat neocortical neurons: blocking activity increased quantal (mEPSC) amplitude across all synapses, while blocking
first raised firing and then let it return toward baseline as amplitudes shrank
. Because the adjustment was multiplicative, relative weights were preserved while firing rate was stabilised
. That mechanism is separate from Hebbian plasticity, and is the cellular reference for any claim that a stimulation effect is bounded or reversed by compensation
rabbit hippocampus, a simulation fitted to visual development, a review-level abstraction, and rat cortical culture
. None was established in an intact awake human, and none was established with a non-invasive

Receptor blockade is the field's main tool for assigning a molecular identity to a human after-effect. Ziemann and colleagues' reference review treats

6.4 State dependence: the same dose, different sign

Silvanto and colleagues state the principle: the behavioural and perceptual effects of TMS depend on the activation state of the targeted neurons at the time of stimulation, and setting that state beforehand can bias which of two spatially overlapping populations is affected
. The strongest human demonstration that prior activity sets the sign is the

result. Siebner and colleagues applied tDCS before 1 Hz repetitive TMS over motor cortex: after anodal tDCS had raised excitability, the rTMS pushed excitability below baseline, and after cathodal tDCS had lowered it, the same rTMS raised it

State can also be read instant by instant. Zrenner and colleagues used millisecond-latency real-time EEG to trigger otherwise identical triple-pulse bursts at either the negative or the positive peak of the

6.5 Variability, and one account reinterpreted as peripheral

Response direction is unreliable between people. López-Alonso and colleagues tested 56 healthy people with paired associative stimulation, anodal tDCS and intermittent TBS: only 39%, 45% and 43% respectively moved in the expected direction, responses were bimodal, and response to one protocol did not reliably predict response to another

At the behavioural level the scepticism is sharper. A quantitative review of 59 studies found no significant effect of single-session tDCS on any cognitive outcome in healthy adults, including working memory and language

The most consequential challenge is a reassignment of level rather than a null. Majdi and colleagues re-examined six published tDCS studies whose effects had been attributed to direct cortical polarization, and argued that stimulation of scalp cranial and cervical nerves could explain them instead (group H-tdcs-plasticity)

after topical anaesthesia blocked somatosensory input

mice, psychedelic-induced synaptic strengthening occurred in granular retrosplenial cortex, whose neurons lack
receptors, and required presynaptic 5-HT2A receptors on anterior thalamic axons instead

or MR spectroscopy markers of glial activation or neuronal injury

"Plasticity" cannot be one edge. The same word covers an in vivo rabbit field potential
, a multiplicative change in quantal amplitude in rat culture

and an MEP change in a human forearm muscle

Direction needs a distribution, not a sign. When 39–45% of participants move the expected way and responses are bimodal

or with the phase at which it is delivered

The first is that a shared

Casarotto and colleagues report that the TRKB transmembrane domain senses cholesterol and that both classical and rapid-acting antidepressants bind a site in the transmembrane region of TRKB dimers, promoting synaptic localization of the receptor and BDNF signalling; mutating the binding site reduced cellular and mouse behavioural antidepressant responses
. The same group extended the proposal to

Both papers combine molecular modelling, cell work and mouse behaviour, and both come from one laboratory

. Until there is one, "antidepressants and psychedelics converge on TrkB" should be held as a single-laboratory structural claim with mouse behavioural support, not as the established mechanism it is often cited as

The mTOR branch comes from the rapid-acting antidepressant work and carries an explicit timescale. modulator and of an mGlu2/3 antagonist alike, which the authors read as a shared requirement for downstream NMDA receptor activation

Immediate-early gene expression is the workhorse

The circuit level has three working terms. Fries' account supplies the reason they are treated as control variables rather than by-products: active neuronal groups oscillate, so their excitability fluctuates rhythmically, opening and closing short windows for receiving input and emitting output, and two groups influence one another effectively only when their windows align at a consistent phase relation

Whether an applied field can impose that phase is a separate, measured question. In ferret cortex,

Awake primate recordings take the claim closer to the human case. Scalp

8.2 What high-frequency deep brain stimulation does to a circuit

Grill and colleagues modelled intrinsically active neurons under extracellular stimulation across frequencies and found that high-frequency stimulation forces output spiking into a regular, essentially variance-free pattern: the cell keeps firing but stops transmitting information

children.value: This section follows one chain from an applied
to a molecule and an outcome, then the argument about whether that chain is a reflex.
Why the chain closes here and not in the head
The neuroimmune branch has something the cortical branches do not: the drive is a nerve that can be reached surgically and stimulated with known current, the
is a molecule assayable in serum, and the anatomy between them is a named set of organs and projections. Borovikova and colleagues' experiment ran from an electrical drive in the rat to hepatic and
. That is the whole chain of section 2 — drive,
, cellular, molecular, system, outcome — in one

Tracey's formalisation treats inflammatory state as something the nervous system senses and regulates in real time, as it regulates heart rate, which makes cytokine concentration a controlled variable and therefore a target for a device
. Pavlov and Tracey's later review sets out which neural, endocrine and immune nodes connect to which, and which of those connections have been addressed experimentally
The inflammatory reflex as it was demonstrated
Borovikova and colleagues reported two experiments in one paper
. In human macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharide
strongly suppressed release of TNF, IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-18, but not IL-10
. In rats made endotoxaemic, direct electrical stimulation of the peripheral
inhibited hepatic TNF synthesis, blunted the peak of serum TNF and prevented shock
. The authors read this as an efferent, parasympathetic anti-inflammatory pathway, distinct from the already-described afferent vagal
and not a dial (section 3), and the record this volume works from does not carry the current, frequency,
. The founding experiment therefore cannot be replicated from what is cited here, and the parametric work that makes a vagal drive reproducible was done later and for a different readout
That parametric work is instructive about how narrow the window is. Recording in rat
across a grid of current amplitude,

, train duration, inter-train interval and pulse width, Hulsey and colleagues found that half-second vagus-nerve stimulation trains drove rapid phasic locus coeruleus firing from 0.1 mA upward; higher current and longer pulse widths raised the firing rate, while pulse frequency changed the timing of the phasic burst without changing the total amount of locus coeruleus activity
. Pulse-locked activity in the mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus, included as a control for non-specific recruitment, appeared only above 1.2 mA
. The same cuff at two amplitudes is therefore two different drives, one of which co-recruits trigeminal afferents
The relay that filled in the middle
The efferent account had an anatomical hole: vagal suppression of splenic TNF requires acetylcholine acting on
on the cytokine-producing macrophages, but vagal fibres do not innervate the spleen and lack the machinery to synthesise acetylcholine there

. Rosas-Ballina and colleagues closed the gap in mice with a non-neural cell. They identified a memory-phenotype population of choline acetyltransferase-expressing T cells in the spleen, and showed that this population is required for vagus-nerve stimulation to inhibit TNF
. The efferent arc thus passes through a lymphocyte that makes the transmitter, and terminates on a receptor expressed by a macrophage

For the graph, this is the section's most consequential single result: an edge in a drive-to-outcome chain can have a non-neuronal cell at one end, so the schema cannot restrict nodes to neurons, axons and brain regions
supplies a second such node type
What the anatomy does and does not support

is where the agreement stops. Martelli, McKinley and McAllen audited the evidence point by point and accepted a great deal of it: that stimulating the cut peripheral end of either vagus suppresses local and systemic inflammation, that the spleen is where systemic TNF is produced and suppressed, that the effect requires
nerve terminals in the spleen and ChAT-positive T lymphocytes, and that α7 nicotinic receptors are essential
. What they rejected is the proposed disynaptic connection from vagus to
does not drive action potentials in the splenic nerve

. Their conclusion separates two claims that the reflex language fuses: the pathway is activatable, electrically and pharmacologically, but it is not the efferent arm of a physiological reflex to endotoxaemia
is therefore not about whether a device works but about what the device is doing to what. One side holds that stimulation engages a hard-wired homeostatic loop that already regulates cytokines

; the other holds that stimulation drives a pathway that exists but is not recruited by endotoxaemia itself, in which case the intervention is closer to a pharmacological trick played on splenic innervation than to closing a natural loop

. What would settle it is electrophysiology rather than outcome data: recordings showing that splenic nerve traffic is driven by vagal stimulation, and that it changes when an animal is made inflamed with the vagus intact. The first has been attempted and reported negative
The human evidence, and what it does and does not establish

The human literature is thinner than the animal literature and differently shaped. Alen's review of vagally mediated control of inflammation in humans finds a large correlational body of work, mostly associations between heart-rate-variability indices and cytokine concentrations, against a much smaller set of experimental studies, with weak causal designs, inconsistent measures of vagal activity and limited target-engagement evidence
The pivotal test is an implant trial. RESET-RA randomised 242 patients with rheumatoid arthritis refractory to or intolerant of biologic or targeted synthetic DMARDs to active or
from an implanted vagus-nerve neuroimmune modulation device for three months, then moved all participants to open-label stimulation to twelve months
response at three months was 35.2% with active stimulation against 24.2% with sham (p = 0.02), and among completers rose to 50.0% at six months and 52.8% at twelve
. Adverse events were similar between arms, and the few related serious events were perioperative and resolved

An eleven-point difference in responder rate, sham-controlled, in a refractory population, is a real result and a modest one, and it does not adjudicate the mechanism dispute: a benefit of this size is compatible with both the reflex account and the activatable-but-not-reflex account
Non-invasive delivery adds a target-engagement problem on top of the mechanism problem. D'Agostini and colleagues gave 66 healthy participants continuous cymba conchae
against earlobe sham, at an individually titrated intensity just below pain threshold, and found no effect on
, salivary alpha-amylase, cardiac vagal activity or respiration, while the task itself produced the expected pupil effects
. The resolution is protocol-dependent. A living Bayesian
of 18 taVNS studies (N = 771) found only anecdotal evidence for a pupil effect overall (
= 1.0), but strong evidence for an effect with pulsed stimulation (g = 0.36, BF10 = 50.8) and strong evidence for the null with conventional continuous stimulation (g = 0.002, BF01 = 21.9)
. That split maps onto the phasic and tonic locus coeruleus regimes of the
, and it makes waveform, not intensity, the decisive parameter

is itself weak: simultaneous locus coeruleus recording and pupillometry in mice gave a monotonic but highly variable relationship, with pupil size predicting only a small fraction of moment-to-moment locus coeruleus activity

Reflex or not, the afferent side is where most vagal fibres are. Prescott and Liberles' review organises vagal sensory neurons by molecularly defined cell type across the respiratory, cardiovascular and digestive systems, and stresses how little is established about signal transduction in vagal afferents and their upstream sentinel cells compared with the external senses

. The practical consequence is that "the vagus" is a heterogeneous bundle of genetically distinct afferent classes, so a cuff or an ear electrode engages a mixture of labelled lines rather than a channel
Gut-brain signalling had been assumed to be hormonal and therefore slow, because no synapse was known between the intestinal epithelium and the vagus

. Working in mice, Kaelberer and colleagues showed that enteroendocrine cells — neuropod cells, in their term — form glutamatergic synapses with vagal afferents and transduce luminal stimuli in milliseconds, linking the lumen to the brainstem across a single synapse
The endocrine limb closes the same way from the other direction. A meta-analysis of 16 randomised controlled trials of prefrontal
in healthy adults found that stimulation reduced the acute cortisol response to a laboratory stressor (
= −0.72), with larger effects for TMS than tDCS and for stimulation delivered before or after rather than during the stressor
. Timing relative to the challenge is part of the dose
act both as circulating endocrine messengers and as locally synthesised neurosteroids enhancing
function by a direct, non-genomic action, so one molecule can be a systemic drive or a local one
Anatomy a graph can stand on

, the SPARC Connectivity Knowledge Base of the Autonomic Nervous System, is the closest thing this level has to a substrate. It is a curated, ontology-backed record of the origins, terminations and routing of autonomic projections between the central nervous system and end organs, assembled from expert input, published literature, textbooks and SPARC datasets, and it generates the connectivity maps on the SPARC portal

. Its neuron populations are named compositionally rather than by opaque label, using the Neuron Phenotype Ontology, which decomposes a neuron type into phenotypes carrying identifiers from community ontologies and reconciled three published cortical neuron classifications with each other and with informal literature names
. Organ and structure identifiers come from a species-neutral anatomy ontology that links species-specific ones, so a structure can be compared across humans and model organisms
What SCKAN contains is population-level structural connectivity: which neuron population projects from where to where, by what route
. It is not a source of stimulation-response or physiological measurement data. Nothing in it says what a 0.1 mA half-second train does to locus coeruleus firing
, whether vagal stimulation drives splenic nerve spikes
, or how large an ACR20 difference an implant produces
. Those are separate claims, from separate papers, with their own species and parameters.
What this level implies for the graph

Three schema consequences follow. First, direction belongs on the edge and not in the node name. Afferent and efferent vagal routes have different anatomy, different transducers and different consequences, and the founding paper distinguishes its efferent pathway from an afferent HPA route in the same nerve
. An edge that says only "vagus → spleen" has lost the claim. Second, sign of effect belongs on the branch rather than on the drive. Vagal stimulation suppresses TNF through one branch
and raises locus coeruleus firing through another
; "vagus nerve stimulation" carries no sign of its own. Third, species must survive import. The molecular chain is rodent with human
, the human mechanism literature is largely correlational
, and the anatomy resource is multi-species by construction
. A graph that imports SCKAN's structural statements alongside stimulation-response claims must keep the
on every edge, which is what an evidence ontology is for
, or it will read a curated anatomical projection and a sham-controlled trial as the same kind of fact.

12.8 What this implies for a graph
Three schema rules follow. First, every edge carries a record of its confound controls: sham type, when blinding was checked, masking, sensory matching, and whether engagement was shown
. Second, a confound is a node with edges to the claims it threatens (auditory input to ultrasound inhibition
, skin input to tACS motor effects
), and rebuttals are counter-edges on that node
. Third, a claim from an unblinded or sham-inadequate study carries a flag, so it can be filtered or down-weighted and is never merged with a controlled one
Pooled estimates need the same treatment: a human ultrasound meta-analysis
inherits whatever confound its inputs carried
, so the graph should record that dependency, not only the pooled number.

15.3 Where nothing exists: protocols and devices

No ontology in this volume's corpus covers stimulation protocols or device parameters adequately. The nearest things are reporting standards and repositories, which say what to write down but supply no identifiers or class hierarchy: the

The large integrative graphs supply the engineering patterns. Hetionet combined 29 public resources into 47,031 nodes and 2,250,197 relationships of 24 types, and showed that path patterns through a typed heterogeneous graph carry mechanistic signal usable for prediction

Where these would lose what this volume needs is in edge semantics. An edge typed only by predicate and endpoints cannot hold a parameter set with units, a nominal-versus-effective pair, a preparation, a confound-control record, or a rival edge that is a competing explanation rather than a duplicate assertion. Automatic extraction compounds the problem, because a mined triple inherits the sentence's ambiguity rather than the study's design
, which is the argument for curating claims by hand as SCKAN and DrugMechDB do
What follows is a starting point, not a specification. It is offered in the expectation that a reader building on this volume will redesign it against their own use case.

Every claim edge, whatever its predicate, carries the same four properties: evidence type
, species and preparation, and a link to its source, plus the dose and state that qualify its sign. An edge without these is not importable
What follows is advice for the reader going to the sources; the builder's own judgement is marked as such.
Consensus and reporting documents are the most efficient entry point to a modality, because they name the parameters a field has agreed matter: RATES, from a three-round Delphi study with 38 experts
, and GRADE for certainty of evidence
. No single journal carries this literature. In this volume's corpus the transducer and relay papers appeared in general journals such as
, and the ontologies and graphs in data and informatics journals
. Following one modality's specialist journal misses most of these.

Searching by modality name returns the recent tier. Three strategies in this volume's sweep returned the seminal tier instead. First, search by the dispute rather than the technique — name the two rivals and the question, as the hypothesis groups in this volume do, and the founding papers appear on both sides. Second, walk citations backwards from a consensus document or a

to the primary studies it grades, then forwards from a founding primary study to the paper that reinterpreted it. Third, search for the mechanism at the level below the one you care about: the ChAT-expressing T cell relay
are found under immunology and gut physiology, not under nerve stimulation, and the intracellular receptor result
under receptor biology rather than under

Four kinds of result deserve scepticism on the evidence collected here. A pooled human estimate whose authors call it tentative, limited by selection bias and incomplete parameter reporting, as the ultrasound meta-analysis does of itself
. A control assumed inert rather than measured, as with the designer ligand that turned out to be converted to a brain-penetrant parent compound
. A structural connectivity statement read as a physiological one, which the SCKAN documentation does not license
. And an automatically extracted assertion used as a fact, since text-mined predications carry the sentence rather than the study design
. In each case the question to ask is the volume's recurring one: what was measured, in what species and preparation, at what dose, and what rival explanation was excluded
